acceptance: Document chosen engine-specific budgeting and override precedence, supported platforms and a measured rationale for Spark non-heap allowance.
Boundary tests exercise small budgets, explicit limits and per-engine/container cap application without exceeding the admitted budget.

context:
2026-11-15 evidence: Spark TPC-DI SF 1 under `make uat-cell` on a 16 GiB host. `bounded_default_driver_memory` sized the heap from the 8 GiB budget less a 3 GiB allowance, yet the JVM footprint reached 7.80 GiB and the watchdog killed the tree at 8.08 GiB after 452 s. The same workload with `driver_memory=3g` finished in 451 s with all queries passing. The 3 GiB JVM-and-Python allowance in `benchbox/platforms/spark.py` is too small for this workload.

description:
Promoted from deferral 1 on heavy-guard-watchdog-20261030: Removed from the guard plan during review; watchdog bounds the tree but engines should fail gracefully before it fires.

## Decision gates
Investigate the measured Spark overhead first: default JVM reached 7.80 GiB/tree 8.08 GiB under an 8 GiB budget; driver_memory=3g completed all 152 queries. Do not assume a universal 3 GiB fix. Implementer proposes per-engine budgeting and precedence; owner approves reduced supported capacity or resource-policy changes.

## Verification rubric
Pass: specify a budget equation including JVM/native/Python/child-process overhead; test explicit user limits versus derived defaults for Spark, DuckDB and applicable JVM/container engines. Boundary tests prove derived caps cannot exceed the admitted tree budget. A bounded Spark SF 1 run demonstrates actual tree memory and graceful engine failure before watchdog intervention when limits are exceeded.

## Additional guardrails
Keep adapter imports lazy. Respect explicit user settings or fail clearly if inconsistent with the budget; never silently raise memory. Do not bypass watchdog or impose unsupported cross-platform container limits.
